# Index funds and fees

The avalanche method pays the highest interest debt first and saves the most money. Automate savings on payday so the money moves before it can be spent. A sinking fund spreads a known future cost, such as a new laptop, across the months before it. A monthly review compares planned and actual spending by category and adjusts next month.

## Pitfalls

Automate savings on payday so the money moves before it can be spent. Keep receipts for deductible expenses in one folder so the yearly tax filing takes an evening. A monthly review compares planned and actual spending by category and adjusts next month. An emergency fund of three to six months of essential costs covers most surprises.

The avalanche method pays the highest interest debt first and saves the most money. A monthly review compares planned and actual spending by category and adjusts next month. Subscriptions creep up quietly, so list them all twice a year and cancel the unused ones. A sinking fund spreads a known future cost, such as a new laptop, across the months before it.

## Steps

- The snowball method pays the smallest balance first and builds motivation with quick wins.
- Keep receipts for deductible expenses in one folder so the yearly tax filing takes an evening.
- A monthly review compares planned and actual spending by category and adjusts next month.
